title: Embedded machine call
statement: Let $y$ be a Boolean input word, let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $m$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet and state set $S$, and let $\iota$ inject the $m$ tape indices into the $k$ tape indices. Choose entry and exit states $\mathrm{en},\mathrm{ex}\in S$, local tape-word assignments $L_0,L_1:\mathrm{Fin}(m)\to\mathrm{List}(\mathrm{Bool})$, and larger tape-word assignments $B_0,B_1:\mathrm{Fin}(k)\to\mathrm{List}(\mathrm{Bool})$. Suppose $B_0(\iota(i))=L_0(i)$ and $B_1(\iota(i))=L_1(i)$ for every $i<m$, and $B_1(j)=B_0(j)$ for every $j$ outside the image of $\iota$. If the run of $M$ from the configuration with input $y$, state $\mathrm{en}$, and tape words $L_0$ reaches the configuration with state $\mathrm{ex}$ and tape words $L_1$ after $t$ steps, and its state is not $\mathrm{ex}$ at any time $u<t$, then the machine obtained by embedding $M$ into the $k$ tapes while retaining its output tape reaches state $\mathrm{ex}$ with tape words $B_1$ after $t$ steps, and its state is not $\mathrm{ex}$ at any time $u<t$.
